q: What do India's draft CCTS targets for iron and steel plants say?
title: CCTS iron and steel draft targets
short: A draft published in the Gazette on 26 June 2026 proposes targets for 255 iron and steel plants, for the 2026-27 compliance year only, against a 2023-24 baseline. For example, it proposes 2.1695 t CO2e per tonne for AM/NS Hazira, down from 2.2701. Comments were open for 60 days.
audience: Steel plants, sponge iron units and their suppliers

ul: G.S.R. 517(E), a draft amendment adding a Third Schedule for iron and steel.
255 plants with registration numbers INSOE0001 onward, from integrated plants to smaller units.
Examples: Tata Steel Jamshedpur 2.3630 to 2.2540; JSW Vijayanagar 2.6178 to 2.4840; Bhilai 3.1487 to 2.9551.

p: It is a draft for public comment, taken up after 60 days. Check the Gazette or BEE's carbon market page for the final version before planning on these numbers.
The fuel, power and production records a steel plant keeps for CCTS also feed its CBAM emissions report for EU buyers, though the two systems draw boundaries differently.

senseible: Senseible keeps a plant's fuel and electricity invoices as dated, fingerprinted monthly records, the activity data its monitoring plan and verifier work from.
